results.title: ECB advances climate and nature work after delivering on 2024 ...
results.content: * ECB remains committed to accounting for climate and nature-related risks within its mandate, in view of growing economic and financial impacts. The European Central Bank (ECB) has further embedded climate and nature-related risks into its core work, by concluding its climate and nature plan 2024-2025. Over the past two years the ECB has refined its assessment of climate and nature-related risks, including the way they inform policy decisions. * **Strengthened integration in monetary policy framework:** the ECB has further integrated climate and nature-related considerations into its policy framework, including the Eurosystem’s collateral framework, and reduced the carbon emissions of the Eurosystem’s corporate bond holdings. These priorities will complement the ECB’s ongoing climate-related actions covering monetary policy, banking supervision and financial stability, such as implementing the climate factor in the Eurosystem collateral framework, further developing scenario and stress test methodologies and ensuring banks’ prudent management of climate and nature-related risks.

results.title: ECB climate factor 2026: New risk discount changes refinancing ...
results.content: # ECB climate factor 2026: New risk discount changes refinancing operations. This indicates that banks should now prepare their collateral pools for climate change, adjust data and valuation models, and plan early diversification toward lower-emission securities. ECB climate factor 2026: New risk discount changes refinancing operations. ## Focus on climate risks: New ECB climate factor changes refinancing operations. In future, the climate factor will act as an additional risk discount on collateral and thus protect the ECB from potential losses in value. The ECB’s climate factor is designed in such a way that it reflects the climate-related transition risks of collateral in a differentiated manner and adjusts the risk discounts to the respective exposure in future. In the remaining preparation time, banks should analyse their collateral pools in detail according to climate risks and establish a classification by issuer, sector and remaining term at an early stage and derive corresponding effects.
